items.title: Security Engineer, RF and Technical Surveillance Countermeasures
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us. DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it. Part of that footprint is the radio spectrum around and inside each site: what transmits there, what listens there, and what the equipment itself gives off. You'll be the engineer who owns that domain end to end: on-site RF monitoring and detection, technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM) and emanations security, from the threat basis through the systems that make the spectrum observable, to sign-off before a site opens. The engineering is in the monitoring and in the tooling that proves the controls hold: the sensors, receivers and their placement, the site baselines, and the detection logic that turns a rogue transmitter or an unexpected emitter into an alert an analyst trusts. External specialist partners do the hands-on sweep and measurement work; you write the scope, direct them on site and decide whether their report stands. The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, sensor health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage. We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones. We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations, construction and legal teams, and directly with site operators and landlords. The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure. Key responsibilities On-site RF monitoring and detection: design and develop the monitoring at each site: sensor, receiver and antenna selection and placement, the spectrum monitoring architecture, site RF baselines and what keeps them current, and detections that reach the team's security monitoring platform as alerts analysts keep trusting Tools, automation and AI agents: build the detection and classification tooling, the instruments and software for checks between sweeps, the findings and evidence records behind them, and the agents that triage alerts and watch sensor health. When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it Technical surveillance countermeasures: own TSCM end to end: sweep cadence by space sensitivity, event-driven triggers such as fit-out, room turnover or an incident, scope and acceptance criteria per sweep, and findings handled with evidence and closure an assessor accepts Emanations security: set the posture for sites: the assessment method, zoning and separation, and shielding, filtering and protected cabling where warranted, written into the team's design and build standards so a site can build to them and an assessor can verify them Wireless and device policy by zone: detect which radios are actually present where (cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, IoT, trunked radio) and produce the evidence that the policy holds on the floor Specialist partners: write the scope and the deliverable standard for sweep and assessment work, direct it on site, and decide in the acceptance review whether a report stands New sites and leases: carry RF and emanations requirements into design reviews, lease terms and pre-opening reviews, and sign off RF and emanations, including the pre-opening sweep and assessment, before a site opens Minimum qualifications Have built at least one RF monitoring or detection system end to end, from receiver and antenna choice through the software that turns captures into alerts Understand RF at the engineering level: propagation, modulation, spectrum analysis and antenna behavior, with hands-on use of the instruments that measure them, such as spectrum analyzers and software-defined radios Have planned and conducted TSCM sweeps yourself and can explain, from having done the work, what a sweep can and cannot find and how an adversary would get past it Have done RF security, TSCM or emanations work hands-on for data centers, critical infrastructure or a large hardware fleet Read and review code, design the data systems behind detection and monitoring tooling, and build automation (often with AI coding agents) using Git and code review Understand compromising emanations and what zoning, shielding and filtering each buy and cost, and write requirements for them that a construction team or a landlord can build to and an assessor can test Direct a specialist vendor without deferring to them: write the scope, check the work, reject a weak report Preferred qualifications Experience assessing compromising emanations and shielding or filtering tradeoffs in a live facility, and applying a formal emanations or counter-surveillance standard, government or commercial (TEMPEST, ICD 705 style construction requirements, or a corporate equivalent) Have built signal classification or spectrum analysis pipelines at scale, or tuned RF detections for a security operations workflow so operators kept trusting them Familiarity with airspace or drone RF detection, and with where it stops and on-site monitoring starts Experience at sites you did not fully control: colocation or multi-tenant facilities, where the RF environment and the walls are not yours alone Have built AI agents or automation that replaced recurring manual security work The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.description: About the Team The Transformation team at OpenAI partners with Finance, Infrastructure, Data, and Engineering to design and scale the business processes and systems that support our growth. Our work combines process design, systems thinking, and operational change to turn fragmented workflows into reliable, repeatable, and well-controlled operations. We work as embedded partners to Finance, Accounting, and Operations, shaping priorities and delivering improvements across core business processes. For compute, our focus is an accurate, connected view of contractual obligations, delivered capacity, usage, and cost that supports sound decisions and repeatable financial operations. About the Role As Program Manager, Compute Transformation, you will lead cross-functional initiatives that connect purchasing, operations, billing, accounting, and financial planning across our compute commitments and our data center initiatives. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of problem definition, process design, integrated planning, and end-to-end delivery. You will work across Compute Finance, Infrastructure Accounting, Capacity Planning, Fleet, Design & Construction, Operations, Procurement, Legal, Data, and Engineering. You will turn ambiguous business problems into clear requirements, drive decisions and dependencies, and deliver reliable processes and systems that make compute and infra spend easier to understand, forecast, reconcile, and control. This role is based in San Francisco, CA, with a hybrid work model of 3 days per week in the office. In this role, you will: - Own an integrated compute and infra transformation plan: workstreams, milestones, critical dependencies, resources, decision logs, and acceptance criteria. Drive execution from problem definition through production adoption. - Map current workflows and design scalable processes from demand planning, contracting, delivery & acceptance, receiving & operations, invoicing, payment, and month-end close. Clarify ownership, handoffs, evidence, and exception paths. - Enable source of truth systems that cover both operational needs and accounting / finance needs for data center construction, operations, and maintenance. - Drive consistent tracking of contracts, tranches, delivery events, and capacity acceptance. Connect committed spend to provisioned, accepted, allocated, and used capacity to support forecasting and financial review. - Coordinate reliable ingestion and normalization of cloud service provider usage, billing, invoice, and delivery data. Establish data owners, completeness checks, and traceability to financial outputs. - Improve compute billing, accrual, and allocation processes through consistent pricing rules, SKU mappings, telemetry and organizational tags, reconciliations, and controlled handling of manual adjustments. - Partner with application, AI, and data engineers to translate requirements into integrations and automation across contract, procurement, compute data, and finance platforms, with monitoring and governed change controls. - Align Infrastructure, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Legal, and Engineering on decisions and dependencies. Manage scope, risks, vendor dependencies, and change requests; escalate with clear options and business impact. - Lead end-to-end testing, UAT, rollout, training, and handoff to operational owners. Define success measures for traceability, data quality, manual effort, exception resolution, close readiness, and adoption. You might thrive in this role if you have: - 8+ years of experience in project or program management, finance transformation, infrastructure operations, or enterprise systems delivery in complex, scaled environments. - Understanding of compute or infrastructure economics and related finance processes, including commitments, usage-based billing, procurement, accruals, cost allocation, and forecasting. - Experience partnering with software and data engineers to define requirements, resolve tradeoffs, test solutions, and deliver changes into production without direct authority. - A strong process mindset and the ability to connect contractual terms, operational events, financial data, and control requirements into a practical future-state design. - Fluency in data dependencies, system integrations, reconciliation, and data quality. Comfort working with analytical teams and tools such as SQL, Databricks, and BI platforms. - Experience improving workflows through automation or AI, with appropriate human review, controls, exception handling, and operational ownership. - Clear, concise written and verbal communication, including executive updates that explain decisions, risks, business impact, and specific actions needed. - Experience driving complex initiatives through ambiguity and organizational change, with clear evidence of hands-on delivery and adoption. items.description: BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system. THE TEAM Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients. Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform. We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work. THE OPPORTUNITY - Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference. - Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks. - Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete. - Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises. - Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance. - Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams. - Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions. - Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production. WHAT YOU BRING - 8+ years operating and evolving production database estates at scale. You have assessed inherited systems, set technical direction and delivered improvements with engineering teams, and can explain how those decisions held up over time. - Strong understanding of high availability, replication and distributed database failure modes. You can explain consistency and availability trade-offs and reason about transaction boundaries and reliable event delivery, including transactional outbox patterns. - Deep, recent hands-on MariaDB expertise, including InnoDB, MVCC and transaction isolation, locking, query optimisation, binary logs and MariaDB GTID replication. You can explain the mechanisms and diagnostic evidence behind your decisions. - Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain. - Strong software engineering skills in Python, Go, Rust or a comparable language. You have personally built and maintained production software or automation for database workflows such as provisioning, failover, online schema changes and self-service operations, using version control, code review and delivery pipelines, with tested failure handling. - Strong low-level Linux, Kernel, storage and networking fundamentals, with the ability to investigate problems beyond the database process. - Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery. NICE TO HAVES - Experience operating databases in containerised, hybrid on-premises/cloud or multi-region environments. Familiarity with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code or GitOps, including their operational trade-offs. - Experience with database proxies or load-balancing layers (MaxScale, HAProxy, ProxySQL, or similar). - Experience with PostgreSQL, Vitess, TiDB, ScyllaDB, ClickHouse or internal database platforms; operational knowledge of Kafka, Redis/Valkey or Elasticsearch/OpenSearch. - Experience in regulated environments or contributions to database engines, operators and other infrastructure software. Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution. We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance. OUR COMMITMENT Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto. We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision. As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws. Stay connected Follow us on X https://twitter.com/krakenfx Learn on the Kraken Blog https://blog.kraken.com/#:~:text=Enter%20your%20email%20address Connect on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/kraken-exchange/ Candidate Privacy Notice https://www.kraken.com/legal/candidate-privacy-notice

items.description: About the Team We are building AI systems that help people tackle complex, consequential work in the legal industry. Law demands careful reasoning, precise language, and sound judgment: understanding the facts, identifying the right questions, weighing competing interpretations, and helping clients decide what to do next. We see an opportunity for AI to help legal professionals work with greater rigor and focus more of their time on the problems that matter most. Our team works across Research, Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market to build AI capabilities and products for legal work. Our customers include the top law firms in the world as well as in-house legal departments of some of the largest businesses in the world. We translate the realities of practice into evaluations, training signals, and useful tools, with the ambition of making AI a trusted part of how lawyers research, analyze, draft, and advise. About the Role We are looking for a Subject Matter Expert in Law who brings the judgment and practical experience developed in a law firm to shaping the next generation of AI. You will help define what excellent legal work looks like, test where our models meet that standard, and turn your findings into better model behavior and product experiences. This is a hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of legal practice and AI development. You will work directly with legal materials, model outputs, evaluation rubrics, and product prototypes. Your expertise will help us tackle some of the hardest questions in legal AI, including how to assess reasoning when there is no single correct answer. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In This Role, You Will: - Define the quality bar for what top-notch legal work looks like, drawing on real matters and the standards lawyers apply to research, analysis, drafting, document review, and client advice. - Design challenging, realistic AI model evaluations with representative facts, source materials, constraints, and deliverables, including cases that test ambiguity, competing arguments, and professional judgment. - Create and review reference work such as research memoranda, contract analyses, redlines, diligence findings, and draft legal documents that demonstrate strong reasoning and practical usefulness. - Develop rubrics that assess legal accuracy, issue spotting, factual grounding, citation validity, jurisdictional context, and the appropriate treatment of uncertainty. - Evaluate model outputs and complete legal workflows, identify recurring failures, and give researchers and engineers specific, actionable feedback supported by examples and corrected work. - Partner with Research on datasets, grading methods, and training tasks or environments that strengthen legal reasoning. Test whether model changes address the underlying problems and improve performance on new cases. - Work with Product and Engineering to identify valuable use cases, prototype workflows, and translate lessons from evaluations into experiences that fit how lawyers actually work. - Collaborate with legal professionals and design partners to refine our standards and test usefulness in practice, applying sound judgment around confidentiality, privilege, data permissions, and professional responsibility. You Might Thrive in This Role If You: - Have practiced law at a law firm, with substantial experience producing and reviewing work for real client matters. We care more about demonstrated judgment and quality of work matter over title or firm pedigree. - Bring deep expertise in one or more practice areas, such as commercial transactions, corporate law, litigation, or regulatory work, and curiosity about workflows beyond your specialty. - Are an excellent legal researcher and writer who can assess authorities, distinguish strong arguments from plausible ones, and explain how facts and context affect a conclusion. - Can make expert judgment explicit: explain why an answer is incomplete, a clause creates risk, or an analysis misses the central issue, and describe what better work would look like. - Enjoy working directly with AI tools, exploring their limits, and testing ideas systematically. You can collaborate closely with technical teams and communicate clearly across disciplines. - Take ownership in ambiguous settings and are willing to build the first version of an evaluation, reference document, rubric, or workflow, then improve it through feedback. - Care deeply about the quality and consequences of legal work, and are motivated by the opportunity to help shape how AI supports the profession. items.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is looking for a talented Designated Technical Support Engineer to join our rapidly expanding, venture-backed startup. We are building a modern knowledge assistant personalized to every employee in your organization, making all information within your company accessible, contextual, and fresh. Our team works hard and plays hard. We are professional, creative, passionate, and most importantly - customer-obsessed. As a trusted technical resource to the customer, you will provide both proactive and reactive support to our growing customer base. By providing the highest level of service to our customers, you will ensure our customer experience is the best in the industry. You will: Own the proactive and reactive support for Glean customers by prioritizing issues for your designated customer(s) Meet with your assigned customers regularly to review issues and develop resolution plans and drive continuous improvement in how you and your Glean teammates provide support to them Be available to your assigned customers via collaborative communication channels consistently to ensure you are providing timely responses and updates on issues Create and maintain customer-specific runbooks and knowledge articles Provide first response, technical troubleshooting, resolution, and follow-through of customer issues and inquiries Assist customers in the configuration, set-up, and verification of new content sources and product features to enable them to realize additional value for their users Educate customers on the use of Glean product features Identify system and user health issues, then create and execute remediation plans while coordinating and updating the customer accordingly Handle customer-impacting alerts which require coordination with customer admin and system resources through resolution Work closely with teams across Glean to drive product, process, and service improvements Drive key improvement projects that will improve the scale and efficiency of support, while providing upgrades to the customers’ support experience Coordinate all support activities with your assigned customer(s), which may include more stringent access and security processes, ensuring you move with high urgency for their issues. Represent the unique needs of your assigned customer(s) with respect to product and security improvements that will improve the customer support experience Please note that this role will be dedicated to select customers and requires additional background screenings/clearances/training/certification, carry & use of customer-provided equipment, and extended on-call shift timing based on customer contractual obligations. About you: Technically curious: you have a never-ending desire to add technical knowledge and skills to your personal toolkit and share those learnings with your peers Fearless: you have an intense need to tackle the toughest customer issues and technically complex issues with the goal of driving customer satisfaction Strong communicator: you are a professional presenter with superior interaction skills with both customers and internal teams Detail-oriented: you are highly organized and methodical, ensuring all issues are managed to completion Data-driven: you utilize metrics and objective measurements to assess success and improvement opportunities for yourself and for the customer experience Key knowledge and skills required: Must-haves: Problem solving: technical problem-solving skills including the ability to troubleshoot and isolate issues to their root cause Ability to debug issues including searching & reading application logs, analyzing stack traces and browser trace files Experience in at least one of the following disciplines: Customer Solutions Engineering, Support Engineering, Professional Services Hands-on experience in at least one of the following: Search technologies, Knowledge technologies, SaaS-based system integrations Experience with Cloud technologies in at least one of the following: Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Amazon Web Services (AWS), or Microsoft Azure Must have experience in troubleshooting REST API issues Working experience on SSO, SAML, and OAuth along with network troubleshooting Able to fully document issues you manage and contribute to the support knowledge base Good-to-haves: Knowledge of SQL/database, Basic Kubernetes, Intermediate/Advanced Linux Experience in using Github, Jira & Confluence Basic knowledge of LLM’s and how GPT works Location: This role is remote but may require flexible working hours. items.description: About the Team OpenAI’s GTM Partnerships team builds a strategic, global partner ecosystem to accelerate customer success, enable responsible enterprise AI adoption, and drive durable growth in support of OpenAI’s mission. We work cross-functionally across Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success to translate strategic partnerships into measurable outcomes for customers. Strategic cloud and technology partners help enterprises adopt and scale AI within their existing technology environments. This role will lead OpenAI’s partnership with Oracle across North America, connecting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), its field organization, and relevant technical and delivery teams with OpenAI’s products and capabilities. You will turn the global alliance strategy into a focused North America business plan and repeatable field execution that delivers customer and commercial impact. About the Role We are hiring a Partner Director, Oracle North America to lead OpenAI’s partner business with Oracle across the region. You will own North America joint business plan, build executive alignment, and activate Oracle and OpenAI field teams to generate qualified pipeline, win strategic opportunities, and drive successful production adoption. You will align regional priorities and execution with the global Oracle alliance strategy. This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role. You will connect senior executive engagement with joint account planning, co-selling, solution and delivery alignment, field enablement, governance, and day-to-day execution. Success requires a strong understanding of how a large, matrixed cloud and enterprise technology organization operates, commercial discipline, technical fluency, and the ability to align teams without formal authority. The ideal candidate has led a high-impact partnership with Oracle, built measurable pipeline and customer outcomes across North America, and knows how to turn alliance strategy into account-level execution and successful deployments. In this role, you will: - Own North America partnership with Oracle, including regional strategy, executive alignment, joint planning, pipeline growth, customer outcomes, delivery quality, and long-term expansion, in alignment with the global alliance. - Develop and execute a North America joint business plan with clear account and industry priorities, investments, decision rights, milestones, and measures of success. - Build trusted relationships with Oracle’s North America cloud leadership, alliance teams, industry leaders, account executives, cloud architects, and customer success and delivery teams, while staying aligned with global stakeholders. - Translate executive priorities into repeatable field execution spanning account mapping, opportunity qualification, co-selling, solution development, technical engagement, delivery handoffs, and escalation. - Shape joint solutions and industry plays that connect OpenAI capabilities with OCI and relevant Oracle data, application, security, and industry capabilities, in coordination with technical and product teams. - Lead joint account planning and strategic customer pursuits with Oracle and OpenAI field teams across North America, with particular focus on complex and regulated enterprises. - Create a clear engagement model for OpenAI sellers and technical teams, including when to involve Oracle, how opportunities are qualified, who owns each step, and how channel conflict is resolved. Coordinate cloud procurement and marketplace pathways where applicable to the customer and partnership. - Partner with Product, Engineering, Solutions, Security, Legal, Finance, and Commercial teams to support complex customer engagements and remove technical, contractual, compliance, and operational blockers. - Build Oracle’s North America field and technical readiness through executive sponsorship, sales enablement, technical training, reusable solution patterns, and disciplined customer deployment handoffs. - Establish regional governance across executive business reviews, pipeline inspection, forecasting, milestone tracking, performance reporting, and escalation, connected to the global alliance operating model. - Set and monitor North America partnership KPIs, including qualified pipeline, conversion, production adoption, customer value, partner readiness, delivery quality, and return on OpenAI investment. - Prioritize OpenAI resources for North America opportunities with the greatest strategic value, commercial potential, customer impact, delivery readiness, and repeatability. - Represent OpenAI in senior partner, customer, and industry engagements with clarity, sound judgment, and strong executive presence. - Build the regional operating model and identify the team capacity needed to scale the Oracle partnership across North America. You might thrive in this role if you have: - Significant experience leading cloud alliances, strategic technology partnerships, ecosystem sales, business development, or enterprise go-to-market programs in AI, cloud, data, SaaS, or enterprise technology. - Direct experience working with Oracle and deep familiarity with its North America cloud organization, OCI field and partner teams, seller incentives, decision-making networks, commercial model, and enterprise customer engagement motions. - A proven record of leading a multi-year partnership or regional alliance business with measurable pipeline, revenue, adoption, deployment, or customer outcomes. - Experience designing and scaling joint operating models across large, matrixed organizations, including governance, account planning, incentives, staffing, delivery handoffs, and escalation. - Demonstrated success shaping and advancing complex C-suite enterprise transformation opportunities from strategy through production deployment. - Strong executive presence and the ability to build credibility with senior Oracle and customer leaders while remaining close to operating details. - Commercial judgment and experience prioritizing investments, qualifying opportunities, managing forecasts, and making clear tradeoffs. - Technical fluency across enterprise AI, OCI and cloud architectures, data platforms, integration, security, governance, and production deployment, with the ability to translate customer needs into clear technical and commercial priorities. - Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to align Sales, Solutions, Product, Engineering, Security, Legal, Finance, Marketing, and Operations without direct authority. - Experience building partner enablement, joint solutions, industry plays, and scalable field engagement models across North America. - Comfort operating in ambiguity and creating structure, accountability, and momentum in a rapidly evolving market. - Excellent written and verbal communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills. - A builder mindset, high ownership, low ego, and a consistent focus on customer value and responsible AI adoption. What success looks like: - OpenAI and Oracle have a clear North America growth strategy, differentiated joint value proposition, executive governance model, and measurable business plan aligned with the global alliance. - Oracle and OpenAI field teams across North America know when and how to engage one another, and qualified opportunities progress through a consistent co-sell and delivery motion. - The North America partnership generates qualified pipeline and converts priority opportunities into secure, successful production deployments with demonstrable customer value. - Joint solution patterns and industry plays become repeatable rather than remaining bespoke. - OpenAI resources are allocated transparently toward the highest-impact opportunities. - Oracle’s North America teams demonstrate growing readiness and accountability across selling, architecture, implementation, and customer success. - The North America partnership earns sustained executive sponsorship and delivers measurable year-over-year growth. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. items.title: Talent Partner
items.description: About MoonPay MoonPay is for builders with something to prove. This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend. 30M+ customers and 500+ ecosystem partners run on us. Licensed in the U.S. Regulated across the UK, EU, Canada, and Australia. AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters. You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together. The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building for what's next, for humans and agents. Recent recognition: Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 . 2nd in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100 The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running Research has shown that women are less likely than men to apply for this role if they do not have experience in 100% of these areas. Please know that this list is indicative, and that we would still love to hear from you even if you feel that you are only a 75% match. Skills can be learned, diversity cannot. Talent Partner, Non-Tech About the Opportunity ✍️ MoonPay is looking for an experienced Talent Partner to help us build exceptional teams across our non-technical functions, including Product, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Marketing and People. Non-technical hiring here is fast-moving, varied and rarely straightforward. You'll own searches end-to-end, working closely with hiring managers to understand what they really need, find the right talent and keep hiring moving. We're looking for someone who knows their market, has strong opinions backed by data, and isn't afraid to rethink the approach when a search isn't working. This is a hands-on role with plenty of ownership. You'll source, advise, problem-solve and close, while helping us continuously improve how we hire. AI should already be part of your recruiting toolkit, and we'll expect you to keep experimenting with how it can make your work smarter and more effective. What you will do Own end-to-end hiring across our non-technical functions, from kicking off a search and mapping the market through to assessment, offer and close. Partner closely with hiring managers and business leaders to understand their teams, define what great looks like and build hiring strategies that work. Find exceptional talent across a range of business and product functions through proactive sourcing, talent mapping and creative search strategies. Bring data and market insight into hiring conversations, spotting where searches are getting stuck and changing the approach when something isn't working. Use AI across sourcing, screening, research, market mapping and reporting, constantly looking for ways to improve the quality and efficiency of your work. Make hiring at MoonPay better. Share what works, challenge what doesn't, and contribute to improvements across our processes, tooling and ways of working. About You 🙋 Significant experience recruiting non-technical talent within fast-moving technology, fintech or high-growth organisations, with a track record of delivering against challenging searches in competitive talent markets. Broad recruitment experience across Product and business functions such as Finance, Legal, Compliance, Operations, Marketing and/or People, with the ability to adapt your approach to different roles, seniority levels and talent markets. Strong sourcing and talent-mapping skills, with the ability to get beyond the obvious candidate pool and find great people others might miss. Comfortable operating in fast-paced, ambiguous environments with a high level of ownership. Data-driven, curious and focused on quality, efficiency and continuous improvement. Confident influencing hiring managers and challenging thinking when needed. Strong practical use of AI in recruiting, plus a deep understanding of cryptocurrency and financial technology. Able to demonstrate how AI has improved your work and speak credibly about the crypto ecosystem and where it's heading. items.title: Principal Engineer, Privacy
items.location_text: Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is working on frontier AI systems that handle sensitive information at enormous scale. How we protect that data, and how we build privacy into our systems rather than bolting it on afterward, is central to our mission of building AI that is safe and beneficial. As one of our principal privacy engineers, you will be among Anthropic's most senior individual contributors on privacy. You will set technical strategy for how personal data is handled across products, research, and infrastructure, and execute the hardest parts of delivering it. You'll work at the intersection of privacy engineering, distributed systems, and AI safety, on problems without established answers. You will lead through influence, quality of thinking, and trust rather than formal authority. Key responsibilities Define and drive technical strategy and architecture for major areas of privacy, spanning product surfaces, research and training data, internal tooling, and multiple clouds Identify and lead the highest-complexity, company-critical privacy initiatives, guiding engineers across many teams. Be comfortable building the most difficult pieces yourself Architect the primitives that make privacy the default and the safe path the fastest one: data discovery, classification, lineage, purpose-based access control, audit, retention, deletion, and export Turn regulatory, contractual, and consent obligations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, the EU AI Act) into enforced, continuously verified technical controls in partnership with Legal, Policy, and Compliance team Anticipate where AI capabilities, regulation, and customer expectations are heading, and position our systems ahead of them Mentor and develop staff and senior staff engineers, raise the bar for privacy design across engineering, and help hire senior privacy talent Represent Anthropic's privacy engineering to customers, regulators, standards bodies, and the research community Minimum qualifications A track record of operating as a Principal engineer or equivalent: setting technical direction that multiple teams adopted, and delivering company-critical, multi-year initiatives Deep experience applying privacy engineering principles in production systems with a large user base, including privacy by design, data minimization, and purpose limitation Experience architecting data governance infrastructure (classification, lineage, access control, retention, or deletion) across distributed systems and cloud infrastructure at scale Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar languages; you are effective writing design docs, making architectural calls, and coding in critical paths Understanding of privacy regulations such as GDPR and CCPA, and the ability to work as a peer with legal and policy experts to turn requirements into technical designs Written and verbal communication that builds alignment across engineering, research, legal, and product teams, up to senior leadership Preferred qualifications Experience building privacy infrastructure or controls for machine learning or AI systems, including training data governance or AI agents Hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (e.g., differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, secure enclaves, secure multi-party computation) Experience establishing or re-architecting a privacy engineering practice under enterprise-customer or regulatory scrutiny Experience briefing executives, auditors, regulators, or enterprise customers on privacy risk, and defending your recommendations under challenge A history of growing engineers into Staff-level and more senior roles Contributions to open-source privacy tooling, privacy research, or industry standards The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $485,000 — $625,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

items.description: This internship offers an exciting opportunity to gain hands-on experience in the fast-paced world of iGaming, learn from industry experts, and contribute to the growth of an innovative gaming company. The Wow As an Intern - Central Gaming, you will play an important role in supporting the visual presentation of our gaming portfolio across multiple brands and markets. Working closely with internal stakeholders and external partners, you will help ensure that game thumbnail requests are managed efficiently from submission through to delivery, while maintaining high quality standards and an organised workflow. Your contribution will help ensure our content is visually engaging, accurately represented, and delivered on time. A taster of what you will be involved with: Workflow Management: Maintain and organise the thumbnail production Kanban board in Jira, ensuring requests are properly tracked, prioritised, and updated throughout their lifecycle. Request Coordination: Submit thumbnail design requests in a timely manner and coordinate their progress, ensuring all necessary information and requirements are communicated clearly. Asset Management: Work with internal stakeholders to obtain and provide artwork, logos, game assets, and other materials required for thumbnail production, subject to availability. Quality Assurance: Review delivered thumbnail assets to ensure they meet brand guidelines, quality standards, and business requirements before approval. Content Administration: Upload approved thumbnail assets to the relevant Jira tickets and maintain accurate documentation of requests and deliverables. Stakeholder Communication: Collaborate with various teams to provide updates, resolve blockers, and ensure requests move smoothly through the production process. Ad-hoc Requests: Support urgent and business-critical thumbnail requirements while balancing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Process Improvement: Contribute ideas and recommendations to improve workflow efficiency, asset management, and overall operational processes. Team Support: Provide operational and administrative support to the Central Gaming team and assist with other projects and initiatives when required. What we are looking for Strong organisational and time-management skills. Excellent attention to detail and a quality-focused mindset. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities simultaneously. Comfortable working with different stakeholders across multiple teams. Familiarity with Jira or similar project management tools is considered an advantage. Interest in gaming, digital content, or the iGaming industry is a plus. Proactive, reliable, and eager to learn in a dynamic environment. What we offer Much like riding a rollercoaster, sometimes life at Betsson can be lightning fast with twists and turns but always FUN! items.title: Learning & Instruction Lead, Academy
items.location_text: San Francisco, New York City, Washington, DC
items.description: About the Team OpenAI Academy helps people develop the skills and judgment to use AI effectively in their work and communities. We deliver practical learning through workshops, online resources, and partners who train others. Our audiences include small businesses, nonprofits, educators, workforce organizations, and people learning to use AI for the first time. The Academy team works closely with Customer Education and Technical Success to bring accurate product knowledge and strong instructional practices into community learning. This role will connect Academy’s audience needs with the training content, product expertise, and enablement practices across those teams. About the Role We’re looking for a Learning & Instruction Lead to own the design, delivery, and ongoing improvement of Academy’s learning programs. You will lead priority workshops, build live and self-paced curriculum, and develop the training, assessments, and credentials that prepare community trainers and advisors to support others. This role combines exceptional live instruction with hands-on learning design and program ownership. You will connect Academy’s audience needs with shared content, competency frameworks, and credentialing standards across Customer Education, Technical Success, and other education teams. You will create polished materials yourself and lead work with external learning partners, taking programs from an initial learning objective through launch and ongoing updates. In this role, you will: - Define competencies and learning paths for priority Academy audiences and community trainer and advisor roles. Map existing content to those needs, identify gaps, and establish clear evidence of product proficiency and readiness to teach or advise others. - Lead in-person and virtual workshops, hands-on labs, and priority Jams; adapt your instruction to different levels of experience and troubleshoot live questions and demos. - Create polished, ready-to-deliver curriculum, presentations, interactive learning experiences, and facilitator and participant resources. - Use AI directly in the design and production workflow to prototype, build, test, and refine training materials. Evaluate new capabilities quickly and turn useful advances into better learning experiences, with careful review for accuracy, accessibility, and reliability. - Partner with Customer Education and Technical Success to adapt shared resources for Academy audiences and keep programs current as products and learner needs change. - Test demos and activities in the accounts and environments learners will use, including access, feature availability, timing, privacy, and appropriate verification of AI outputs. - Own training and credential requirements for community trainers and advisors, aligned with shared OpenAI frameworks and Academy audience needs. Lead the development of assessments and credentials with internal experts and external learning partners, setting clear standards for quality and evidence of learning. - Prepare and coach instructors and mentors through train-the-trainer sessions, practice, and reusable guidance. - Partner with Academy program and partnerships colleagues to scope learning experiences that fit the audience, available staffing, and delivery capacity. - Manage external learning partners and coordinate internal contributors to develop, launch, and improve Academy programs. Own priorities, quality, and the overall learner experience. - Use learner work, feedback, and recurring product friction to improve programs and inform relevant internal teams. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have a track record of designing and delivering practical adult learning, customer education, technical enablement, or workforce training. - Have taken a learning program from design through launch and ongoing operation, coordinating content, assessments, learner access, and external contributors. - Are an exceptional live instructor with a track record of leading engaging, hands-on sessions, explaining complex ideas clearly, reading the room, and adapting in real time for beginners and experienced participants. - Use ChatGPT and Codex confidently to build, test, and refine practical demonstrations and learning resources, with sound judgment about accuracy and limitations. - Are an excellent learning designer who can translate an audience need into clear objectives, well-sequenced instruction, meaningful practice, and useful evidence of learning. - Have a portfolio of fully polished training resources that you personally created and brought to delivery quality, combining strong writing, visual judgment, instructional design, and attention to detail. - Have coached instructors or partners and can define observable standards for teaching readiness and quality. - Bring the judgment to distinguish a beginner workshop from a session requiring deeper engineering expertise and involve the right specialists. - Work well across content owners, product experts, program managers, and external partners, with clear ownership and follow-through. - Care about expanding access to useful AI skills and have experience adapting learning for varied professional and community contexts. Helpful experience - Train-the-trainer programs, facilitator networks, or partner-led education. - Learning assessment, accessibility, localization, or delivery to nonprofit, small-business, education, and workforce audiences. - Familiarity with APIs, agents, and evaluations to support collaboration with technical instructors and appropriate builder content. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. items.title: Internship - HR People Ops EMEA
items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As an HR People Ops intern on the People Operations team at Mistral AI, you will support our EMEA people operations in a hands-on, fast-moving environment. This is a great opportunity to discover the full scope of People Operations in a fast-growing AI company while contributing to our expansion across Europe. You will work closely with the People Ops team, assist with day-to-day operations, and take ownership of concrete projects, such as improving our HR documentation and helping coordinate onboarding for new joiners across EMEA. items.title: Member of Technical Staff (TPM, Compute)
items.description: Perplexity is looking for a technical program manager to own how we plan, bring online and run the GPU compute behind every product. Perplexity serves Ask, Computer and API traffic on GPU capacity across multiple cloud and neocloud providers, and demand shifts with every new customer, product launch and model release. Working across engineering, research, Finance and providers, you’ll forecast how much compute we need and when, bring new capacity into production, and own how the fleet performs today, driving fixes when reliability, utilization or cost fall short. The ideal candidate knows GPU fleets, handles technical and commercial details, and is energized by building a function with little precedent. OUR MISSION Perplexity’s mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating. Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending. Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they’ve learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality. Integrate: they must interact with the world as it is to drive change and adoption. True leaders do not simply build something and hope. They must have armies of agents and workers who can constantly work in millions of small ways. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Partner with Finance on the compute demand forecast, 3–12 months out, driven by customer growth, model releases, and post-training and evaluation plans rather than trend lines - Turn the forecast into decisions with Finance and engineering leadership on commitments and budget, checking that new capacity fits the plan before we commit - Bring new capacity online and lead transitions, from contract to production, including provider onboarding, acceptance criteria, migration and decommissioning - Build a single, trusted view of the fleet: capacity, cost, allocation, and uptime, reliability and utilization by provider and workload - Drive daily utilization, reliability and cost-efficiency as core metrics, reclaiming idle capacity and surfacing trade-offs rather than letting them become side effects - Own inference and compute requests end to end: triage and resolve GPU, deployment and quota requests from teams across Perplexity, and build self-serve paths so routine requests no longer need a person in the loop - Manage compute provider relationships, with scorecards and regular reviews of reliability, support and delivery, and use that data to shape how we work with providers over time - Partner with engineering, research, and finance teams on capacity decisions that match the different needs of training, batch inference and real-time production inference - Build the operating system for compute: the processes and tooling to request, plan, allocate and track compute, with clear owners QUALIFICATIONS - 6+ years of technical program management, capacity planning or infrastructure operations in cloud environments, leading programs across teams and vendors - Direct experience with GPU or accelerator fleets across training and inference workloads - Experience working directly with cloud or neocloud providers on reserved capacity, capacity commitments, onboarding or vendor performance management - Experience with infrastructure cost modeling, unit economics or cost attribution in partnership with Finance - Technical depth in cluster management, scheduling and orchestration, and the data skills to build forecasts and dashboards yourself - The judgment to surface hard trade-offs and communicate them clearly from engineers to executives - Thrives in a small, agile team; has initiative and desire for ownership without much precedent to lean on

items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE As a Design Operations Manager (DesignOps), you will sit within Mistral's Product Operations function, with a focus on streamlining the operations of the design team. You will own how the Design team operates as a system — its cadences, its rituals, its coordination, and the connective tissue that lets designers focus on design. This role exists because a design org at our scale needs someone whose full-time job is the operating system itself: defining it, holding it, and continuously tuning it so the team runs with a heartbeat rather than on ad-hoc heroics. You will own the team's weekly and quarterly cadences — from leadership syncs to planning, retros, and share-outs — and establish how we track work, surface it outward, and make decisions. You'll design the forums where decisions get made and recorded, keep the rituals that create alignment, and aggressively cut the ones that are just overhead. Equally, you are the bridge across the org. You will coordinate the interlocks between Brand and Marketing for upcoming launches, and between Product and Product Design for the build pipeline — so interdependencies are understood and planned for, not discovered at the last minute. You will partner closely with marketing, PMs, engineering, GTM to align design work with go-to-market timing and surface what's shipping before it ships. This is a team-of-one role with a founding design-ops mentality. You will build the discipline from scratch, automate repetitive coordination with AI where it helps, and coordinate people where it matters. You report to the Head of Product Operations, working day-to-day with the Head of Design and the design team. WHAT YOU WILL DO - Define the operating system of the design team — the cadences, forums, rituals, and source-of-truth that keep the team aligned and moving forward. - Own the weekly and quarterly cadences, from leadership syncs and critiques to planning, retros, and headcount-cycle inputs. - Coordinate the Brand × Marketing and Product × Product Design interlocks so design work is surfaced with enough lead time and dependencies are planned, not discovered late. - Establish how the team tracks and shares out work — a single source of truth for status, and the forums where design is made legible to the rest of the org. - Design and hold decision-making forums so decisions get made, recorded, and not relitigated. - Separate ritual from overhead — keep the cadences that create alignment and cut the ones that are just tax. - Automate repetitive coordination, reporting, and tracking with AI so the team spends time on design, not admin. - Bring the wider Product Operations toolkit to the design team — data and analytics for transparent reporting, structured feedback loops and early-access programmes, and launch coordination that aligns design work with product release cycles and go-to-market timing. - Partner with marketing, PMs, engineering and GTM to align design work with go-to-market timing and surface what's shipping. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 6–10 years of experience in design operations, product operations, program management, or a chief-of-staff role within a creative or product organization. - A founding design-ops mindset — you've built operational disciplines from scratch, not just maintained inherited ones. - Comfortable automating with AI tools to remove repetitive overhead, while equally skilled at coordinating people and building coalitions without authority. - Strong systems thinking — you design repeatable rhythms and processes, not just run meetings. - Design literacy — enough background to have felt the pain designers feel and to be credible with the team. - A make-it-happen attitude: positive, bias to action, unblocks rather than escalates. - Excellent communication and synthesis skills — you turn scattered signals into a shared source of truth. - Ability to thrive in ambiguity and define your own scope in a role with no playbook and no team to delegate to. WHAT WE OFFER We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.
